question.worked_solution:
To solve the equation $\sqrt{5x-9}=x-1,$ we raise both sides to the power of $2.$  This allows us to get rid of the radical, and gives us a quadratic equation that is easier to solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5x-9} & =x-1 \\ {(\sqrt{5x-9})}^{2} & =(x-1)^{2} \\ 5x-9 & ={x}^{2}-2x+1 \\ {x}^{2}-7x+10 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2x)+(-5x+10) & =0 \\ x(x-2)-5(x-2) & =0 \\ (x-5)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =2,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that in square root equations, we should always check the obtained value(s) to ensure that they are actually solutions of the original equation.

- First, we check whether the obtained value $x=2$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5(2)-9} & \overset{?}{=}2-1 \\ \sqrt{1} & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed, the value $x=2$ does satisfy the original equation.

- Second, we check whether the obtained value $x=5$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5(5)-9} & \overset{?}{=}5-1 \\ \sqrt{16} & \overset{?}{=}4 \\ 4 & =4\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed, the value $x=5$ does satisfy the original equation.

Therefore, the solutions of $\sqrt{5x-9}=x-1$  are $x=2,\,5.$
